races.name: Visit Perth Museum Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Biggles
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old prominent racer for Tom Lacey and Stan Sheppard who has shown ability at 2m on Good ground (placed in similar conditions twice from five runs), though form figures of 25 suggest inconsistency and the competitive front-end scenario could expose him if he uses too much energy chasing the two natural leaders.

runners_data.name: Hawthorn Road
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 5-year-old hold-up type returns from 93 days off which is a notable fitness query, and all three recent runs came on Soft ground, making this Good surface a minor unknown; however the structural position at the back suits perfectly in a contested-pace race if the layoff hasn't blunted his sharpness.

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's horse is a genuine hold-up type by nature but the surplus of sit-and-wait runners in this field means it will likely be forced to race closer to midfield than ideal — this positional compromise tempers confidence slightly, though its best recent form includes a second and a third at 2m-plus on decent ground.

runners_data.name: C'Est Pour Moi
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old natural front-runner for Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies, ridden by a 7lb claimer, with both prior runs at 2m on Good ground finishing 6th and 9th — the pace duel with Crackalackin is the core risk, as neither run suggests the gate-to-wire form to see off a proper contest.

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole's 4-year-old front-runner has a more encouraging form profile including three runs on Good ground at 2m with a second and third among them; returning from 88 days off is worth noting but the hg:p tag and prior pattern suggest a horse that can roll along at the front and stay competitive.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Adam Nicol's 4-year-old is a hold-up horse with a modest form string (one sixth on Good at 2m, no wins from 5 runs) and returns after just 22 days; Ryan Mania's booking is a positive, but the bare record on comparable ground (0W1P from 7 runs in similar conditions) leaves questions about whether it can capitalise even with the ideal structural position.

runners_data.name: Try Them
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride for Patrick Neville on this 4-year-old prominent racer whose form includes a second at 2m on Good and a pair of fifths, making it arguably the most interesting prominent type in the field; the 44-day absence is unremarkable and Hughes's tactical awareness is an asset if he can place the horse just off the front-running duel without getting embroiled in it.

races.paceDynamic: C'Est Pour Moi and Crackalackin are both confirmed front-runners, meaning early possession will be contested rather than gifted — neither is likely to simply slot in behind the other, so there will be genuine early pressure on the front end over Perth's 2m trip. That honest gallop plays directly into the hands of hold-up and midfield horses who can travel economically off the pace and pick up late, rather than prominent types who may find themselves racing up against the leaders throughout. Biggles and Try Them hold prominent positions and will need to balance energy expenditure carefully, while the three hold-up types — Hawthorn Road, Tracker Issue, and St Just In Time — are best placed structurally, though the field holds more sit-and-wait runners than can realistically fill the back of the field, meaning St Just In Time is unlikely to get as far back as it would prefer and is shown in midfield as a consequence. The overall shape favours a patient, hold-up profile that can exploit the pace set by the two leaders and produce a sustained late run — honest gallop at the front should ensure the race is truly run, rewarding stamina and finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If C'Est Pour Moi and Crackalackin trade blows up front and set a genuine, sustained gallop that softens the leaders before the home turn.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other's energy through the race, leaving a clear opening for horses held up behind to swoop late with fresh legs over the final flight; Good ground at Perth suits a true-run race where stamina edges out position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Settles, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of C'Est Pour Moi or Crackalackin dominates from the start without a sustained duel and is allowed to dictate a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: With an uncontested lead the front-runner controls the pace and has energy in reserve for the final straight, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to produce enough momentum late; the lone leader gets a soft lead and converts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong but burns out before the final flight, allowing a prominent runner just off the leaders to stay on into a weakened pack.
scenarios.body: Biggles or Try Them, travelling just behind the duel without over-committing, inherit the lead at a crucial point and grind to the line on Good ground that poses no concern for either; their prominent style is rewarded without being fully exposed early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fails, Pace Steadies
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners conspire to set only a modest tempo that renders the closing kick of hold-up horses ineffective.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race would leave Hawthorn Road and Tracker Issue with too little time to build momentum from the rear, and the position in the field becomes a liability rather than an asset; St Just In Time, unable to get far back anyway, is least affected but still below peak tactical efficiency.

watchPoints.text: C'Est Pour Moi and Crackalackin — watch whether either concedes the lead immediately at the start; if one dominates unchallenged by the second flight the pace scenario shifts dramatically toward Scenario B and changes the race shape entirely.

Hawthorn Road — a 93-day absence combined with a switch from Soft to Good ground means any sign of sluggishness or slow warm-up behavior in the paddock should downgrade confidence in its ability to produce a sustained late run.

St Just In Time — watch its position in the early stages; if it is forced into a midfield spot rather than at the rear the horse is racing out of its natural role, and a closer-than-usual position on a front-loaded pace could compromise its finishing effort.

Try Them — Brian Hughes will likely try to find the sweet spot just off the two front-runners, and if he can achieve that berth by the end of the first circuit without being crowded, this horse's Good-ground form at 2m makes it worth monitoring as a prominent alternative to the hold-up types.

Biggles — at age 9 and dropping back to 2m after a pair of runs over 16 furlongs, watch whether Stan Sheppard opts to press close to the leaders early; if he does, energy expenditure in a duelling race could blunt Biggles in the final stages given the horse's recent record of fading (16th, 7th) over shorter.

races.name: QuinnBet Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over similar trips give him strong credentials here, and Sean Bowen's presence for the Bowen yard adds confidence; his P-style suits a race where the leader may leave a gap to track, and 48 days since his last run looks routine given that form trajectory.

runners_data.name: Follow Your Luck
runners_data.note: Uncontested lead virtually guaranteed, but the 177-day absence for Patrick Neville's yard is a genuine fitness query on chasing debut — Hughes will have to manage the fractions astutely to ensure the tank doesn't empty before the last fence on this 2m4f trip.

runners_data.name: Glen To Glen
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old still learning his trade over fences, his H-style and headgear (p, first time) flag a horse connections are managing; recent form shows no placing in his last three and a refusal (R) last time, making him the most fragile profile in the field despite the Good going posing no concern.

runners_data.name: Ras Kassar
runners_data.note: Recent run just 20 days ago keeps him fit and race-sharp, and his best handicap form figures (2nd and 4th) have come on Good ground; David Pipe's yard is not firing in the short-term (0/0 in 14 days) but the horse arrives here fresher in conditions that suit and holds each-way claims from a P position.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Consistent but limited, Kinbara Firstdraft has finished between 4th and 7th in all five recent starts including two on Good — Leonard Kerr's runner has no win from similar flat-form races and his H-style in a slow-run race is the least advantaged profile in this field; headgear (t) is familiar and won't transform him.

races.paceDynamic: Follow Your Luck is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and faces no meaningful pressure for the lead, meaning Brian Hughes can dictate terms at a pace entirely of his own choosing on Good ground over 2m4f at Perth. Tamarind Bay and Ras Kassar will likely press forward into prominent positions behind him, creating a small, bunched front group rather than a strung-out procession, but neither is likely to seriously challenge Follow Your Luck for the front. Glen To Glen and Kinbara Firstdraft will operate from further back, needing the pace to be strong enough to bring them into play in the straight. This race shape — a single uncontested leader controlling the tempo — strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles, as the lack of pace pressure reduces the likelihood of a late collapse that would reward hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Follow Your Luck bowls along uncontested and sets a true but manageable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Hughes settles Follow Your Luck into a comfortable rhythm, controls the fractions, and arrives at the last with enough in reserve to hold on; the lack of any pace rival means no horse drags the tempo beyond sustainable. Front-runners and prominent racers who can travel close to the pace benefit most, as the race develops into a test of jumping accuracy and stamina at a consistent clip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Follow Your Luck's long absence (177 days) tells late and a prominent tracker picks him off.
scenarios.body: Follow Your Luck's fitness after nearly six months off surfaces as a vulnerability in the final half-mile, leaving the door open for a horse tracking closely throughout; Tamarind Bay's sharp recent form — two wins from his last two outings on Good — makes him ideally placed to capitalise from his P-style position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to set up a late run and the closers find clear daylight.
scenarios.body: Glen To Glen or Kinbara Firstdraft would need a genuinely strong gallop to burn out the principals, which is unlikely with a single front-runner able to self-regulate; Glen To Glen's headgear (p) and moderate recent form record further limit confidence in a late flourish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners are impeded by jumping errors or fall, fundamentally reshaping the contest.
scenarios.body: With only five runners, a single faller or unseater mid-race could dramatically alter positions and suits horses still standing in a prominent spot; Tamarind Bay's clean jumping record and consistent form give him the edge in a disrupted scenario, while Ras Kassar's headgear (ht) hints at a horse that can switch off and adapt.

watchPoints.text: Follow Your Luck has been off the track for 177 days — watch whether Brian Hughes is able to maintain fluency over the fences late on, as a fitness-related jumping error in the final circuit could open the race up entirely.

Glen To Glen's recent refusal (R) last time out combined with first-time hood (p) makes him a jumping risk to monitor early; a loose horse or interference from a jumping blunder by this horse could affect the small field significantly.

Tamarind Bay carries 164lbs as top weight alongside a 48-day break — watch how Sean Bowen positions him in the early stages, as any sluggishness leaving the tape could see him concede too much ground to Follow Your Luck to claw back.

With only five runners on Good ground at Perth, the pace Follow Your Luck sets in the first mile will be the key variable — watch the split at halfway to assess whether the fractions are slow enough to keep the hold-up horses in contention or whether the race is already effectively over.

races.name: IM Group Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a recent win on Good; carries 168lbs and has Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore behind them, but the trainer's 14-day record reads 0/2 and the style-fit tag suggests this may be a shape where the role comes easily but the weight bites late.

runners_data.name: Harry
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer with back-to-back wins at 2m and 2m2f, a 9-year-old in fine nick for David Pipe; most of his form comes on Soft/Heavy but the Good conditions here are not a red flag given his class, and Rian Corcoran's claimer allowance is meaningful with 166lbs aboard.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: 10-year-old veteran for Nicky Richards who has placed twice on Good and shapes ideally to sit just off the pace; sim-going figures show 9 runs on comparable surfaces with one win and seven places, suggesting a model of consistency rather than brilliance.

runners_data.name: Dream's Ka
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old hold-up type with a striking recent record of two wins and two seconds on Good ground over 2m; Ryan Mania's booking is eyecatching and Katie Scott's 16-day trainer window shows active runners — the step up to 2m4f is the one question mark given all her form is at 2m.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Soul
runners_data.note: Exciting recent record of four wins from similar Good-ground conditions and a horse who is a natural prominent type; the 69-day break and a disappointing last run (0) need explaining, but if fresh and right Brian Hughes takes this sort of mount seriously.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: 10-year-old hold-up specialist who has placed in 8 of 13 runs on Good; ridden by an amateur claimer in Gregor Walkingshaw (10lb), which helps offset the weight, though at this age and over a trip slightly beyond his sharpest form he needs the scenario to unfold for him.

runners_data.name: Follow Charlie
runners_data.note: Won most recently on Good ground over 2m and is a natural hold-up type — trainer R Mike Smith had a winner in the past 14 days (1/13) which is a live stable flag; the 4-runner in his recent form string on similar ground suggests he handles this trip in the right setup.

runners_data.name: O'Faolains Glory
runners_data.note: Genuinely a prominent-styled horse by nature whose recent form over Soft ground shows two wins on comparable surfaces, but the 146-day absence and the redistribution into midfield because the field is stacked with pace-setters both chip away at his chances here.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type by inclination whose recent form is built on Good-ground placements at shorter trips — the 19-day turnaround is a positive and the trainer is in form, but her redistribution note reflects that she's being squeezed even further back than her natural position, which makes a winning run harder to construct.

runners_data.name: Annie Agnew
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who is a natural front-runner by style, but the 85-day absence combined with being displaced from her preferred prominent position by the crowded pace scenario means her effectiveness is structurally compromised; the Good-ground form (8/9 sim-going runs) is solid but the role is the issue.

runners_data.name: Struth
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse for the Russell/Scudamore yard whose last five runs have all been fifth or sixth finishes; Derek Fox is a high-quality jockey and the weight is the lightest in the race at 147lbs, but there is no win or place on this going combination and the redistribution tag signals that even his rear-group role is compromised in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Lets Mingle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m4f handicap hurdle at Perth, and with no genuine rival to push them along, the early fractions on Good ground are expected to be controlled and sustainable rather than searching. Harry and Summergrounds are legitimate prominent types who will look to sit just off the pace, but the field contains a glut of horses who want to be up with the pace — O'Faolains Glory, Annie Agnew, and Cosmic Soul are all natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy those slots, meaning several will race out of their preferred position further back than ideal. The field holding more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate means O'Faolains Glory and Annie Agnew are the ones most likely to be squeezed out of their natural slot, with Harry and Summergrounds better placed to land the prominent berths behind Lets Mingle. A controlled pace set by Lets Mingle over 2m4f on Good turf strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and strike at the second-last, or hold-up horses with a strong staying finish — but the dominant shape here rewards those who can sit handy in the slipstream and produce a clean jump at the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mingle Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle dictates a steady gallop throughout and prominent stalkers get a clean run from two out.
scenarios.body: Lets Mingle sets a comfortable tempo, allowing Harry or Summergrounds to travel smoothly in their wake and produce a timely challenge at the second-last hurdle; on Good ground at this trip, horses who race with the pace and avoid traffic carry a decisive advantage over those forced wider or deeper into the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate through the middle section and a staying horse gets an uninterrupted run from the final bend.
scenarios.body: Dream's Ka has the form in the book over 2m on Good and is effective as a hold-up type when the gaps come at the right time; Garde Des Champs and Follow Charlie both have winning form at this level and could exploit a strong finishing burst if the pace bunches the field late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle's lead evaporates under pressure and the field compresses into a sprint finish from three out.
scenarios.body: With several displaced prominent types forced into midfield, horses like Cosmic Soul or O'Faolains Glory who find themselves racing out of their preferred role could benefit if chaos at the front creates a wall of opportunity; this scenario is tempered by the REDISTRIBUTED tags on O'Faolains Glory and Annie Agnew, meaning their chance here is structurally discounted.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle's controlled gallop is slow enough to leave them with plenty in reserve for the run-in.
scenarios.body: Lets Mingle has winning form on Good ground and at 2m, and if the pace is entirely on their terms they could simply outstay a field that has left its charge too late; this outcome is the least likely given the weight carried and the quality of the hold-up horses tracking through.

watchPoints.text: Lets Mingle's weight (168lbs) must be monitored from the second-last — if Jack Power starts to ride with urgency before the last, the front-runner is vulnerable to anything travelling easily behind.

Dream's Ka's trip upgrade from 2m to 2m4f is the key unknown; Ryan Mania will be looking to hold up and produce her run from the final bend, but if the extra distance blunts her finishing kick she may find the line coming too soon.

The cluster of O'Faolains Glory, Annie Agnew and Cosmic Soul all competing for prominent positions in the early stages could produce racing room issues on the first circuit — any bumping or interference between these three should be flagged for stewards' inquiry.

Harry's entire career form is on Soft or Heavy ground; Good at Perth is drier than anything he has encountered, and while his class is not in question, his jumping and jumping-off point should be watched closely from the third hurdle onward.

Follow Charlie's trainer R Mike Smith has a recent winner in the 14-day window (1/13) — horses from small northern yards who show this stat in handicap hurdles at Perth can be underestimated in the market.

races.name: Malcolm Group Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a win and two places from five Good-ground starts, including a recent course win over 20f; Brian Hughes is a high-class booking and this 3m trip stretches her 20f form but she handles Good ground fluently and her natural position close to Burgundy Man's pace is a significant structural asset.

runners_data.name: October Hill
runners_data.note: Holds course form and his 14 runs on similar ground show seven places — consistent rather than flashy; rider Rian Corcoran claims 5lbs which helps the burden, the tongue-tie is retained, and 20 days since his last run suggests freshness; travels prominently and should find a comfortable early position behind Burgundy Man.

runners_data.name: Just Oot
runners_data.note: 427 days off the track is a significant flag for this hold-up type whose best form came over shorter trips on Good ground; Susan Corbett has only two runners in the past 14 days and this is a tough return ask over 3m, though a placed effort at 21f on Good ground shows stamina is not an issue in principle.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Genuinely in the form of his life having won back-to-back races at 24f on Good ground and a 34-day turnaround keeps him fresh; an 11-year-old who knows his job, he races from hold-up and his recent Good-ground record (12 runs, 3 wins, 6 places) is the standout statistic in the field — the 3m trip is new but his stamina profile is strong.

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: Good recent trainer form (2 from 31 in 14 days) and a tongue-tie is applied; his true running style is hold-up but with three genuine closers in this field he is pushed forward on the map — racing out of his natural position discounts his chance in a shape that depends on a fast-finishing surge, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects that structural constraint.

runners_data.name: Ceol Draiochta
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has pulled up twice and finished out of the frame in all five recent starts; a hold-up type with no Good-ground wins or places on this card, and the step to 3m looks ambitious given she has never won over any distance hurdling.

runners_data.name: Drumlee Myth
runners_data.note: Won his latest over 22f on Good ground which is an obvious positive for this stamina test; a natural hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map means he may not get the ground-saving, late-charging race he needs — STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers expectations, though his recent win keeps him in contention if the pace is genuinely testing.

runners_data.name: Magic Gloves
runners_data.note: A prominent type whose last six runs show four finishes of tenth or worse; headgear (tongue-tie) retained, 69 days off the track, and a move up to 3m from 20f is speculative — Derek Fox is a strong jockey booking but the raw form figures make it hard to get excited about his prospects here.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: Three runs on Good ground all at Perth, including a recent third over 20f, show course familiarity but a drop back from 22f last time and the step to 3m is untested; a prominent runner who will naturally find a position close to Burgundy Man, and Peter Kavanagh's ride is the key tactical interest.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and race-shaper; headgear (tongue-tie and hood) retained, rated just 79 and a record of pulls-up and poor finishes in recent form suggests his role here is to set the pace rather than win it — trainer Smith has one winner from 13 in the last 14 days, which is modest but not alarming.

runners_data.name: Quinnfinity
runners_data.note: A four-year-old flagged for fading in finishes whose entire form profile on Good ground — three runs, zero wins or places — offers minimal encouragement; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, with STYLE_FIT of 0.90 and a tendency to fade meaning this 3m trip on Good ground looks very much against him.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner, 3-mile handicap hurdle over Good ground at Perth, and with no rival willing or able to genuinely challenge him for the lead, he can dictate at a measured, controlled tempo from the outset. That sustainable gallop — set by a horse rated just 79 and carrying 142lbs — is unlikely to produce an extreme pace that burns off the field, meaning the race will not become a true test of stamina until the final circuit. Prominent runners Dolly Dior, October Hill, Magic Gloves, and Fortunes Dawn will sit in behind at comfortable distances, tracking a pace they can live with, which fundamentally advantages horses travelling well and close to the action in the middle stages. The race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile — horses able to press forward from a handy position off an uncontested lead, quicken when asked turning in, and sustain their effort to the line over a trip that suits on ground that is genuinely Good. The field holds more hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear; Broken Ice, Drumlee Myth, and Quinnfinity are genuine closers but are mapped into midfield, meaning those who can naturally race prominently and organically find a good position will hold a structural advantage over these redistributed types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Burgundy Man Leads, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the prominent runners track him comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Dolly Dior and October Hill, travelling close to the pace throughout, are ideally placed to pick up when the leader's advantage shrinks on the run to the final hurdle, with Dalileo and Drumlee Myth capable of threading through from just off the pace if the tempo is honest enough to bring them into it late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man and one prominent companion, most likely Dolly Dior or Fortunes Dawn, gradually edge clear of a strung-out field as hold-up types are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow pace on the first circuit rewards bold jumping and positive riding from the front, with horses that have jumped well and travelled fluently throughout simply outstaying rivals who cannot quicken from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Finds Dalileo
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated over the final mile, turning a 3-mile Good-ground hurdle into a true test of staying power.
scenarios.body: Dalileo, a consistent performer at 24f on Good ground with three wins at that trip in recent form, is the profile that benefits most from a race run on genuine merit where class at the trip counts; Drumlee Myth's win at 22f on Good also keeps him involved.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Denied, Chaos Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or departures reshuffle the field entirely and the natural hold-up types — Broken Ice, Quinnfinity — are gifted a race run at an extreme, unsustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability shape because those tagged hold-up horses are mapped out of their natural position and the single front-runner Burgundy Man is unlikely to produce a blistering gallop; if chaos intervenes, Broken Ice's course experience gives it the best chance of the redistributed trio to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Burgundy Man's jumping must be monitored from the outset — if he makes a serious error early, the race loses its only pace-setter and the field may bunch dangerously, creating congestion for the prominent runners immediately behind.

Dalileo's back-to-back wins have come at 24f; the step to 3m (24 hurdles) is a genuine unknown for an 11-year-old and Callum Bewley must judge his energy expenditure carefully from a hold-up position on what could be a slowly-run first circuit.

Just Oot's 427-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — watch how she travels through the early stages; a horse returning from that length of time away can switch off or, conversely, over-race, and either outcome over 3m on Good ground is damaging.

Dolly Dior and Fortunes Dawn are both prominent types with Perth course form — if they race too keenly against each other in the early stages chasing Burgundy Man's measured lead, both could be vulnerable in the final half-mile of a 3m contest.

Broken Ice, Drumlee Myth, and Quinnfinity are all natural hold-up types shown in midfield on this map — watch whether any of them actually do try to close on Burgundy Man early, which would confirm a genuinely competitive pace and open the race up for the true stamina profiles like Dalileo.

races.name: Scone Estates Stone Of Destiny Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: The Last Cloud
runners_data.note: Joint-top OR of 129 and a win on Good over 16f, but has not run for 168 days — a significant fitness query for a horse trained by Patrick Neville whose yard is 0/5 in the last 14 days; tracks prominently and needs to reproduce her best after a long absence.

runners_data.name: Filibustering
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good at Perth over 16-17f make him the class act of the pace battle; Harry Derham's yard is 0/1 recently but Filibustering's course form is outstanding and he wears a tongue tie — he is the most dangerous of the three front-runners if allowed to set his own fractions.

runners_data.name: Squeezebox
runners_data.note: Remarkable recent form with three wins from five over 16f on Good, giving him a sim-going record of 10/15 which stands out; Stan Sheppard rides and wears headgear (tongue tie and hood), and at OR 119 he is well-handicapped if his style of settling off the pace allows him to pick up a field that has burned itself out.

runners_data.name: Medieval Gold
runners_data.note: Trainer Patrick Neville 0/5 in the last 14 days is a concern, and the last five runs have come on Soft ground — his one similar-going effort produced only a second at 14f on Good; runs prominently but steps back sharply in trip compared to recent starts and the absence of 172 days needs to be respected.

runners_data.name: Fidendum
runners_data.note: Won two of his last three on Good over 16f and posts a strong sim-going record of 7/9; Nick Slatter claims 3lb which is a meaningful advantage at this level, and as a genuine front-runner he will be closely involved in shaping the race, though the pace war with Filibustering could cost him late.

runners_data.name: Nap Hand
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (two seconds, a third, a fifth in last five) rather than a winner; apprentice Fern O'Brien claims 5lb and trainer Chris Gordon is 1/2 in the last 14 days — his hold-up style makes him a genuine late finisher but he needs the leaders to have done enough to open the door.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 16f most recently but is likely to be crowded out in a three-way pace battle and may be racing under pressure from the start; Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's team is 0/2 recently, and if Scriabin loses his position he drops out of his natural role entirely.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is unavailable in this strongly-run race — pushed into midfield by the sheer volume of pace, his OR of 104 is the lowest in the field and even a well-run race may not deliver enough of a battlefield for him to come home strongly enough to matter.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Filibustering, Fidendum, and Scriabin — will clash for the lead from the off on Good ground over Perth's sharp 2m, making a strong, honest gallop virtually inevitable. Filibustering has won twice over this course and distance on Good and is likely to assert most aggressively, with Fidendum and Scriabin pressing alongside, ensuring there is no let-up from the first hurdle. This relentless early tempo will stretch the race out and drain the leaders' reserves, shifting the advantage decisively toward horses who can settle in behind and deliver a sustained late run — the Prominent-to-Midfield profile is best placed to exploit a race that will be truly run. The field holds more front-running types than can all secure a clean lead, and of the three, Filibustering — on the back of two recent wins here — and Fidendum appear most likely to actually dictate, with Scriabin at risk of being crowded out early and dropping away from his natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Breaks Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Filibustering, Fidendum, and Scriabin fight for supremacy from the off and set a truly punishing gallop that cracks them all before two out
scenarios.body: The three front-runners burn each other up through a fierce pace duel, leaving them emptying in the home straight and handing the race to a well-positioned hold-up or midfield horse delivering from off the pace. Squeezebox and The Last Cloud, both comfortable on Good ground and capable of sustained finishes, are ideally profiled to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Filibustering establishes a clear, controlled lead early and is allowed to manage the pace without a war developing
scenarios.body: With his two wins over this exact course and distance on Good, Filibustering is equipped to dictate at a tempo that suits him rather than destroying himself, and his higher OR of 129 gives him the class edge over the other pace-setters. If he gets a solo lead through the early stages, he has the speed and jumping ability to hold on through the final two flights before the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace settles into a fair rather than brutal gallop and the race is decided by a quick burn from the second-last hurdle
scenarios.body: A controlled but honest pace plays into the hands of prominent racers who track the leaders at close quarters and kick when the front-runners crack — Medieval Gold and The Last Cloud sit comfortably in that profile. Medieval Gold's win at 17f on similar ground shows class at this level, and The Last Cloud's OR of 129 represents the joint-highest rating in the field, making her dangerous if produced at the right moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Over Toil
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses the field and the race degenerates into a stamina test that rewards the deepest stayer off a slow early crawl turning into a sprint
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely given three confirmed front-runners virtually guaranteeing an honest gallop, and Pure Gold — the only true hold-up type — has been redistributed to midfield precisely because there is no space at the rear in this race shape. Nap Hand has finished second twice recently and could stay on late, but a true late-closers' race requires conditions this card is unlikely to produce.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Filibustering, Fidendum, and Scriabin immediately fight for the lead at the flag — if all three are locked together through the first half-mile the pace will be brutal and the entire race shape shifts toward hold-up and prominent runners.

The Last Cloud has been off 168 days; watch her in the paddock and early in the race for signs that the layoff has blunted her sharpness, as her prominent style leaves no margin for a slow jumper returning from a break.

Scriabin's ability to secure a clean lead is in doubt with Filibustering and Fidendum present — if he is shuffled back or has to race wide under pressure from the start, his chance is materially diminished regardless of his recent win.

Pure Gold is the only true hold-up horse in the race but is effectively forced to race in midfield; if the gallop is so fierce that even midfield becomes the winning position, his redistribution could inadvertently suit him, but his low OR of 104 limits upside.

Medieval Gold's yard (Neville, 0/5 last 14 days) and 172-day absence combine as a significant stable watch — any market move for him given those flags deserves attention as an insider confidence signal.

races.name: Brooks Macdonald Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Sean Bowen but struggling for form (5P-73P), has placed twice in 15 similar-going starts without a win; at 10 years old and 168lbs over 3m, will need a dramatic pace collapse to threaten, with the tp headgear not reversing a losing run.

runners_data.name: Button Rock
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m5f on Good at Perth, and with Derek Fox aboard is a natural prominent racer who could sit perfectly on the heels of the front-running duel; four wins from seven on similar going makes him the most straightforward beneficiary if the leaders soften each other.

runners_data.name: Le Malin
runners_data.note: 12-year-old partnered by the 3lb claimer McParlan, but showed his class with a recent 2m win on Good and has four placed efforts in 12 similar-ground starts alongside that win; a genuine hold-up type who will need the front two to truly empty themselves over 3m before he can land a telling blow.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with four wins from 15 similar-going runs, all on Good, and has won over both 23f and 26f at Perth — the horse to beat from the front if he can see off Mcgregors Charge without cost; the blinkers underline his need to be on the pace, and Nick Scholfield has him in form (two wins from last five).

runners_data.name: Collingham
runners_data.note: Finished fourth last time on Good and boasts four wins from 13 similar-ground runs, but his true style is deep hold-up and the redistribution places him in midfield against his nature — wearing a visor and carrying 161lbs, the structural mismatch tempers his chance even in a pace-collapse scenario.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner from Polly Gundry's yard, wearing a tongue-tie; OR of 79 is the lowest in the field and the form reads PP7-54, which suggests he is more likely to set the pace for rivals than to sustain it over 3m — his chief role is as a pace-maker who shapes the race for others.

runners_data.name: Ballydangan
runners_data.note: Peter Kavanagh takes the mount on this genuine hold-up type returning from a 149-day absence, with only two placed runs from six on Good going and no win on the surface; racing out of his natural back-of-the-field position adds another layer of difficulty to an already uncertain comeback effort.

races.paceDynamic: Edgewell and Mcgregors Charge are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 3m Perth circuit, creating a genuine two-way duel for supremacy rather than any lone, uncontested gallop. On Good ground at Perth, that kind of honest, front-two battle tends to sustain a solid tempo throughout, which historically at this course compresses the field and brings hold-up horses into play in the closing stages — but only if they can get close enough by the home turn. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape naturally accommodates: Collingham and Ballydangan are genuine back-of-the-field runners who have been mapped to midfield positions simply because there is no room at the rear, meaning their redistribution reduces their effectiveness in a shape that demands a true stalking role. This race shape — a contested early pace between two genuine leaders at a fair, honest gallop — favours a prominent racer who settles just behind the duel and picks up the pieces when one of the front two capitulates, with pure hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edgewell Dictates, Button Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell edges ahead of Mcgregors Charge by the second circuit and sets a controlled but honest pace that softens his rival.
scenarios.body: Edgewell, proven over this course and distance on Good going (4W in similar conditions), drives clear from the front while Mcgregors Charge fades; Button Rock, naturally prominent, sits a length or two off and produces his finish over this longer 3m trip, having won last time out over 2m5f on Good.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Burn, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the duel between Edgewell and Mcgregors Charge is more intense than anticipated and drains both runners in the final mile.
scenarios.body: With both leaders giving way approaching the last, Le Malin — versatile, consistent on Good ground and showing a recent win on this surface — arrives from a covered midfield position to take advantage, with his strong placed record at this trip making him the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mcgregors Charge Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Mcgregors Charge, racing off a low OR of 79 and wearing a tongue-tie, outfoxes Edgewell by dictating a steadier gallop.
scenarios.body: A modest pace set by Mcgregors Charge rather than a shared duel reduces the attrition on the leader and allows him to conserve enough energy to hold on; Button Rock, drawn into a chase from a prominent position, is best placed of the chasers but may find the winner difficult to reel in over 3m at this weight differential.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers From Deep Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely severe and Collingham or Ballydangan can overcome their redistributed map positions to produce a true late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both redistribution disadvantages to be irrelevant — a low-probability outcome given neither Collingham nor Ballydangan is a natural midfield operator and both are effectively racing out of role; Ballydangan has been off 149 days adding further uncertainty, and Collingham's visor run last time produced a pull-up.

watchPoints.text: Edgewell and Mcgregors Charge will fight for the lead from flag-fall — watch whether Edgewell immediately asserts or whether Mcgregors Charge forces a genuine battle, as the intensity of that early duel determines the entire race shape.

Button Rock is the key danger to Edgewell in the closing stages — if Derek Fox has him travelling freely just off the pace through the second circuit, he becomes the most dangerous prominent racer with the form to confirm it.

Ballydangan has been absent 149 days and is a true hold-up type mapped into midfield; watch for any signs of ring-rustiness or reluctance to settle in an unnatural position, as either would effectively end his involvement early.

Le Malin's 3lb claimer McParlan reduces his burden to 163lbs effective — if the front-runners do burn each other out, watch whether he has enough position turning for home to capitalise, as his hold-up style means he needs everything to go right over 3m.

Perth's 3m circuit can be unforgiving in the final half-mile on Good ground — watch the pace through the back straight on the second circuit as the point where Mcgregors Charge typically drops away, signalling whether this is a true-run race or a tactical test.
